en: O Agni, you have made me the bearer of the powerful Soma, that I may sacrifice in the assembly; shining toward the gods, I harness the pressing-stone— O Agni, for the sake of well-being, take pleasure in this body of mine.
We have performed the sacrifice facing eastward; may the song increase. With fuel and with reverence, they have honored Agni.
They have ordained the sacrificial assemblies of the sages from heaven; for the wise and powerful one, they have sought a path.
The wise one, of purified will, has conceived the joy; by birth he is the close kinsman of heaven and earth.
The gods found the beautiful Agni within the waters, in the labor of the sisters.
The seven mighty rivers have magnified the fortunate one; he was born white and ruddy in his greatness.
Like mares rushing toward a newborn foal, the gods, at his birth, gazed upon Agni with wonder.
Spreading his brilliance through the mid-air with radiant limbs, purifying his will by means of the sages' filters,
and clothing himself in light, he measures out the vast and perfect glories of the waters as they circulate around his life-force.
He has entered those who do not eat, the undeceived ones, the mighty daughters of heaven, unclothed yet not naked.
Here, the ancient ones, though youthful, dwelling in the same womb, have conceived a single embryo—the seven voices.
His piled-up masses, assuming every form, are spread out in the womb of ghee, in the flow of honeyed streams.
Here stand the swelling cows; the two great, united Mothers of the wondrous one are present.
O Son of Strength, being borne along, you have shone forth today, assuming brilliant and impetuous forms;
streams of honey and ghee drip down where the Bull has grown great through poetic wisdom.
From birth he discovered even his father’s udder; he released its streams and its milky flows.
Though moving in secret with his auspicious friends, the great ones of heaven, he was not hidden from view.
He bore the embryo of both the father and the progenitor; alone he sucked at many swelling breasts.
O two wives of equal kin, protect this manly, pure one for both of you among men.
In the wide, unconfined space, the great one has grown; the waters have indeed gathered around the glorious Agni.
As the domestic lord, Agni lay in the womb of Truth, in the activity of his sisters who are kin.

Like a horse bearing the prize in the encounter of the great [waters], he is eager to be seen by his son, he whose luster is bright; he who as progenitor brought forth the ruddy cows, Agni, the most manly child of the waters, the mighty one.
The forest has brought forth the lovely child of the waters and the plants, the blessed one of manifold forms.
Even the gods have come together in spirit; they have honored him, the most praiseworthy, the powerful one, as soon as he was born.
Mighty indeed are his radiances; like brilliant lightnings, they attend Agni Bhr̥jīka.
Having grown up as if in secret within his own seat, they milk out immortality in the boundless expanse.
I praise you with oblations as a sacrificer; desiring your friendship and favor, I praise you.
Together with the gods, measure out protection for the singer, and guard us with your domestic splendors.
O Agni, our excellent leader, may we, as your followers, possessing all riches and impelled by glorious seed,
overcome the godless enemies who attack us.
O Agni, you became the banner of the gods, the delightful one who knows all poetic wisdoms. As the domestic lord, you have caused mortals to dwell; as a charioteer, you go straightway to the gods.
The immortal king has sat down in the dwelling of mortals, accomplishing the sacrificial rites.
With his face anointed with ghee, Agni has shone forth widely, knowing all poetic wisdoms.

Come to us with your auspicious friendships, O Great One, hastening with your mighty aids. Bestow upon us abundant wealth that crosses over all difficulties, and grant us a glorious portion accompanied by fair renown.

These ancient births of yours, O Agni, and these new ones, I have proclaimed to you, the primordial one. These great libations have been prepared for the Bull; in birth after birth, Jātavedas has been established.
In birth after birth, Jātavedas, established by the Viśvāmitras, is kindled incessantly. May we abide in the favor of that one worthy of sacrifice, and in his auspicious goodwill.
O powerful one, O wise Agni, bestowing gifts, place this sacrifice of ours among the gods. O Hotṛ, grant us abundant nourishments; O Agni, win for us great wealth through sacrifice.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, rich in wonders and most enduring.
May there be to us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours be ours.
For Vaiśvānara Agni, who increases the cosmic order (*ṛta*), we fashion our prayer like purified clarified butter;
with their thought, the human priests and those who offer praise fashion him as the Hotṛ priest from of old, just as a craftsman fashions a chariot with his axe.
By his very birth, he caused both heaven and earth to shine; he became the praiseworthy son of his two parents.
Agni is the bearer of oblations, ageless, well-disposed, the invincible guest of the people, and rich in light.
By the power of their skill, within the ordinance of the victorious one, the gods generated Agni through their insights.
Shining with luster and great light, I address him like a steed, desiring to win the prize.
Desiring to win, we choose from the delightful one that which is most excellent, the shameless prize, worthy of song;
Agni, the gift of the Bhr̥gus, the eager one with the insight of a seer, ruling with his divine radiance.
For the sake of bliss, the people who have trimmed the sacrificial grass and raised their ladles have placed Agni at their head here— he who is renowned for his strength,
the radiant one belonging to all the gods, the Rudra of sacrifices, who perfects the offerings of the skillful.

O Purifier, O Radiant One, for around your dwelling at the sacrifices, the men who have trimmed the sacrificial grass, O Hotṛ, desiring your service and seeking kinship with you, wait upon you, O Agni; bestow wealth upon them.
He filled the two worlds and the great sky when he was born, as the skillful ones sustained him.
That sage is led forth for the sacrifice like a steed, set in place for the winning of booty.
Worship him who accepts the oblation, the one skilled in the sacrifice; honor the domestic Jātavedas.
Agni, the charioteer of the lofty *ṛta*, the all-beholding, has become the domestic priest (*purohita*) of the gods.
The immortal *uśij* purified the three fuel-sticks of the mighty Agni as he moves around;
of these, they assigned one for the enjoyment of mortals, while two entered the world of the kinsman.
The human offerings have sharpened him, the sage of the people and lord of the clans, like an axe for its edge.
He goes to the heights and the depths, busily active; he has established his seed within these worlds.
Having been born, he stirs within the bellies like a roaring lion;
Vaiśvānara, the immortal one of broad radiance, bestowing goods and treasures upon the donor.

Vaiśvānara has ascended to the vault of heaven, the back of the sky, as of old, being celebrated by those of good intent. Like the ancients, generating wealth for living beings, he, the watchful one, goes around the common path.
The observer of cosmic order, worthy of sacrifice, the inspired singer, the one to be praised, whom Mātariśvan established as a dweller in heaven—
him, Agni, whose path is variegated, whose hair is golden, the brightly shining, we implore for new-found prosperity.

Like the pure one on his course, the impetuous, the beholder of the sun, the banner of heaven stationed in the radiant realm, awakening at dawn— Agni, the head of heaven, the irresistible, the prize-winner, him we implore with great reverence.

We ever seek for wealth that delightful, pure, guileless Hotṛ-priest, the friend of the house, worthy of praise, and beheld by all people— a sightly marvel like a chariot, established by Manu, for the sake of beauty.
To Vaiśvānara, whose form is broad, they offer inspired songs as jewels so that he may go to his firm foundations;
for the immortal Agni honors the gods, and thus he has not violated the eternal laws.
The wondrous messenger moves between the two worlds, the Hotṛ priest seated as the domestic chaplain of man.
Agni, impelled by the gods and rich in wisdom, adorns his vast dwelling day by day.
The sages have magnified Agni with their thoughts—the banner of sacrifices, the accomplisher of the assembly—in whom they have concentrated their works and their songs;
in him the sacrificer desires blessings.

The father of sacrifices, the lord of the wise, Agni, the measure and the path of the officiants, has entered the two worlds of manifold forms; the sage, beloved by many, is glorified through his manifestations.

The gods have established here that Agni, who is like the moon, whose chariot is radiant, whose laws are golden, who dwells in the waters, who finds the light of heaven, who plunges forward, who is swift, who is encompassed by powers, and who is impetuous and most glorious.

Agni, spreading the sacrifice—richly adorned through the thought—with the gods and the human race, moves as a charioteer between them with successful offerings; he is the swift master of the house, the dispeller of curses.
O Agni, sing praises for us so that we may have good offspring and long life; swell with vigor and shine forth nourishment upon us.
Quicken our vital powers and the great ones, O watchful one; you are the yearning desire of the gods, the wise skill of inspired songs.

The men ever praise with reverence and with hastening prayers for his increase— the lord of the people, the mighty guest, the director of thoughts, the eager one of the sacrificers, the knower of all beings, the observer of the rites.
The radiant god Agni, the joyous one, has encompassed the dwellings with his power, he whose chariot is auspicious.
May we, in our home, honor the ordinances of him who possesses abundant nourishment, with well-fashioned hymns.

O Vaiśvānara, I yearn for your powers by which you became the finder of heaven, O far-seeing one. As soon as you were born, you filled the worlds and the two realms; O Agni, you encompass all those things by your own self.
By his own skillful work, the solitary sage has brought forth a great song from the wondrous deeds of Vaiśvānara;
magnifying both his parents, Agni was born from Heaven and Earth, who possess abundant seed.

At every kindling, be well-disposed toward us; at every offering, bestow upon us the favor of wealth. O God, bring the gods here for the sacrifice; as a friend, O Agni, worship the friends with a well-disposed mind.
O Tanūnapāt, whom the gods— Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni— worship three times a day, day after day,
do thou make this sacrifice of ours honey-sweet for him who honors thee and whose source is clarified butter.
The prayer, containing all desirable things, goes forth first to worship the Hotṛ of the *iḷā* offering;
with homages, one approaches to praise the Bull. May he, the most excellent sacrificer, being impelled, perform the sacrifice for the gods.
Upward has your path been made at the sacrifice; upward have the flames risen through the regions.
Or rather, the Hotṛ has sat down upon the navel of heaven; we spread the sacrificial grass, wide enough for the gods.
Choosing the seven priestly offices with their minds, impelling all things, they come according to the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
Adorned with heroes, born at the assemblies, they have entered this sacrifice in their many forms.
When the two Dawns, near at hand, are being praised, they smile with their bodies though they are of different forms,
so that Mitra and Varuṇa may be pleased with us, and Indra with the Maruts by their great powers.
I honor the two divine Hotṛ-priests first; the seven nourishers rejoice according to their own nature.
Praising the *ṛta*, they speak only of the *ṛta*; as guardians of the vow, they meditate upon the sacred law.
May Bhāratī, in harmony with the Bhāratīs; Iḷā with the gods; and Agni with men;
and Sarasvatī with the Sarasvates—may these three goddesses sit down upon this sacred grass (barhis).
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, being gracious, release for us that generative seed which nourishes;
from which a hero is born—skillful in action, highly dexterous, one who sets the pressing-stones in motion, and a lover of the gods.
O Lord of the Forest, release [the offering] toward the gods; let Agni, the immolator, prepare the oblation.
May he, the most truthful Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice, for he knows the generations of the gods.
Come hither, O Agni, being well-kindled, on the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods!
Let Aditi, the mother of noble sons, sit upon our sacrificial grass; let the immortal gods rejoice in the Svāhā-call!

Agni, the wise seer and the pathfinder of the sages, has awakened, shining forth against the dawns. With broad radiance, kindled by those seeking the gods, the bearer of oblations has thrown open the doors of darkness.

Agni has grown strong before us through the praises, songs, and hymns of his worshippers—he who is worthy of homage. Delighting in the many manifestations of the Eternal Order (Ṛta), he has shone as the messenger at the dawning of the Dawn.
Agni has been established among the human tribes, the offspring of the waters, fulfilling his purpose through the cosmic order (*ṛta*) like Mitra.
Desirable and worthy of sacrifice, he has taken his place upon the high ridges; indeed, the inspired sage has become the one to be invoked by our hymns.
Agni becomes Mitra when he is kindled; Mitra is the Hotṛ, Varuṇa is Jātavedas;
Mitra is the vigorous Adhvaryu, the friend of the household; Mitra is [the lord] of the rivers and of the mountains.
He guards the beloved summit of the bird, the enemy’s foremost station; the mighty one guards the course of the sun.
At the navel, Agni guards the seven-headed one; lofty, he guards the delight of the gods.
The Ṛbhu fashioned for himself a praiseworthy and beautiful name, he the god who knows all ways.
He guards that very place, the skin of the grain and the footstep rich in ghee, O Agni, never being heedless.
Agni has taken his place at the ghee-rich womb, wide-extending and longing, he who longs [for it];
shining, pure, lofty, and purifying, he makes his two parents ever new again and again.
As soon as born, he grew by means of the plants when the sprouts nourish him with clarified butter;
like waters beautifying themselves on a downward slope, Agni has found wide space in the lap of his parents.
Extolled with fuel, the mighty one has shone forth from the height of heaven, at the navel of the earth.
Agni, worthy of praise as Mitra and Mātariśvan, shall bear the gods hither for the sacrifice.
The lofty Agni, becoming the highest of the luminous realms, propped up the firmament with his kindling wood,
when Mātariśvan brought forth from among the Bhṛgus the oblation-bearer who was dwelling in secret.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, full of wondrous power and most enduring.
May there be for us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours be with us.
O singers, being urged by your thoughts, lead the one who seeks the gods toward the gods as you worship them.
Carrying the sacrificial oblation for Agni, the ladle, rich in strength and flowing with ghee, goes forward to the east.
At your birth, you filled the two worlds, O most worshipful one, and even now you have surpassed them.
By your greatness, O Agni, let your seven-tongued carriers speed forth from both heaven and earth.
Heaven and Earth, and the worshipful gods, establish you as the Hotṛ priest for the household,
when the human tribes, seeking the gods and offering oblations, praise your bright flame.
The great one is seated firmly in his place, cherished between the two mighty worlds, heaven and earth;
the two wives, never-ageing, uninjured, yielding their milk together, are the two cows of the wide-striding one.
O Agni, your vows are great, belonging to the Great One; by your wisdom you have stretched out the two worlds, heaven and earth.
At your birth you became the messenger; you, O Bull, are the leader of the peoples.
Or rather, yoke to the pole with the harness-ropes the two long-maned, ruddy steeds that drip with ghee, belonging to the *ṛta*;
then, O God, bring hither all the gods, and make our sacrifice successful, O Jātavedas.
Even from heaven thy lights have shone forth; thou shinest after many dawns as they break.
O Agni, when the gods praised the waters in the forests that thou didst burn with desire, they extolled thee, the joyous Hotṛ-priest.

Whether they are the gods who rejoice in the wide mid-air, or those who dwell in the luminous realm of heaven, or those helpful, worshipful ones who are easily invoked— the chariot-horses that have drawn near, O Agni.
O Agni, come hither with these [gods] on a single chariot, or on various chariots, for your horses are powerful;
bring the thirty-three gods accompanied by their wives according to your wonted way, and rejoice!
He is the Hotṛ priest for whom even the two wide worlds, Heaven and Earth, praise every sacrifice for its increase.
Facing forward like two well-established paths at the rite, they stand firm—the two who uphold the cosmic order (*ṛta*), true to the one born of *ṛta*.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, most wondrous and most constant.
May there be to us a son, a progeny that continues the lineage; O Agni, may that benevolent thought of yours be with us.

Those who have ascended from the nourishment of the white-backed one have entered the two parents and the seven voices. The two parents, dwelling around, move together; they glide forward to bestow long life upon our gaze.
The milch-cows dwelling in heaven, the mares of the bull, the goddesses, have approached him, carrying sweetness.
In the seat of *ṛta*, the one cow moves around you who bring peace, following your path.
They have ascended him, becoming well-governed; the wise husband, the finder of wealth among riches, has mounted them.
He of the dark back, with his many-formed countenance, has caused them to dwell upon the food of the brushwood.
The strengthening waters carry the great, ageless, and firmly established offspring of Tvaṣṭṛ;
flashing with his limbs in the place of assembly, he has entered the two worlds as if they were one.

They know the favor of the ruddy bull, and they rejoice under the command of Bradhna; they who are far-shining, bright-shining, and radiant, for whom the hymn is a mighty host and a source of nourishment.
And so they proclaimed aloud the cry of praise to the two great parents;
when the bull, at the conclusion of the night, has grown strong according to his own nature for the singer.
Seven sages, together with five Adhvaryus, guard the beloved, hidden track of the Bird.
Moving forward, the ageless bulls rejoice; for as gods, they have followed the ordinances of the gods.
I honor the two divine Hotṛ-priests first; the seven nourishers rejoice according to their own nature.
Praising the *ṛta*, they speak only of the *ṛta*, as guardians of the vow, contemplating the sacred law.
The many reins, easy to guide, act like stallions for the great steed, for the wonderful bull;
O divine Hotṛ, most sweet and wise, bring hither the great gods and the two worlds, Rodasī.
The dawns have shone forth with wealth, providing nourishment for the sacrifice, accompanied by eloquent speech and beautiful light.
And so, O Agni, by the greatness of the earth, forgive even the sin that has been committed; grant us great favor.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, wondrous and most enduring.
May there be to us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, let that benevolence of yours be with us.
O Lord of the Forest, those seeking the gods anoint you with divine honey at the sacrifice.
Whether you stand upright and bestow wealth here, or whether you dwell in the lap of this Mother Earth, grant us riches.
Sitting before the kindled fire, winning for yourself the imperishable prayer that brings heroic sons, drive far away from us all lack of understanding; rise up for our great good fortune!
Rise up, O Lord of the Forest, upon the height of the earth;
being measured with a perfect measurement, bestow splendor upon the one who bears the sacrifice.
A youth, well-attired and enveloped in splendor, has come; he becomes even more excellent as he is born.
Wise poets, devout in mind and seeking the gods, lead him forward with their thoughts.
Born, he is born again on the auspiciousness of days, increasing at the assembly and the sacrifice.
The wise, skillful ones purify him with their inspired thought; the seer, seeking the gods, raises his voice.

O Lord of the Forest, those whom the god-seeking men have set up, or whom the axe has carved out— you gods, dwelling in the light and standing firm, may you bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny.
Those which have been hewn upon the earth, set up with uplifted ladles— may they,
the winners of the field, win for us what is desirable among the gods.

May the Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus, the excellent leaders, Heaven and Earth, the broad Earth, and the Mid-region—may these gods, being of one accord, protect the sacrifice; may they raise high the banner of the rite.
Like swans moving in rows, the sacrificial posts have come to us, clothed in brilliance;
being raised up by the sages in the east, they go as gods to the path of the gods.
Like the horns of horned animals, the sacrificial posts with their head-pieces appear upon the earth;
hearing us at the invocation of the priests, may they protect us in the contests for booty.
O Lord of the Forest, grow with a hundred branches; may we grow with a thousand branches—O you whom this sharpened axe has brought forth for great good fortune.
O friends, we mortals have chosen you as our god for protection—
the Son of the Waters, the blessed one, of splendid luster, the swift victor, the peerless.
When you, O Agni, desiring the woods, went to your mothers, the waters— that turning back of yours is not to be forgotten, that though you were far away, you have come here.
You have grown beyond the harsh; thus indeed you are well-disposed. Others go forth one after another, while others sit around, in whose friendship you are established.
Having passed beyond all failures and beyond all perpetual pursuers,
the observant and guileless ones found him who had taken refuge in the waters, like a lion.
Like one who has run his course by his own nature, Agni was thus hidden away;
Mātariśvan brought him hither from afar, having churned him out for the gods.
O bearer of oblations to the gods, mortals have seized you,
since you, O most youthful one, protect all human sacrifices through your wisdom.
That auspicious power of yours, O wondrous one, reveals itself even to the simple-minded,
when the cattle gather around you, O Agni, as you are kindled at the close of day.
Offer oblations to him who performs the sacrifice well, the sharp one with purifying luster;
serve the god with obedience—the swift, agile, ancient messenger who is worthy of praise.
Three thousand, three hundred, and thirty-nine gods have honored Agni;
they have sprinkled him with clarified butter, strewn the sacrificial grass for him, and then established him as the Hotṛ priest.
O Agni, the wise mortals kindle you, the god and sovereign lord of the peoples, at the sacrifice.
At the sacrifices, they praise you, O Agni, as the officiating priest and the invoker;
shine as the guardian of the Cosmic Order within your own abode.
He indeed who offers to you, O Jātavedas, with fuel—O Agni, he gains great heroic power; he prospers.
May Agni, the banner of the sacrifices, come hither with the gods; being anointed by the seven hotṛ-priests, he approaches for the sake of the one who offers oblations.
Bring forth a lofty, ancient word for Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, who,
like a wise ordainer, bears the lights of inspired songs.
May our songs increase Agni, from whom the praiseworthy one was born—
the beautiful one, for the sake of great strength and wealth.
O Agni, as the most excellent sacrificer at the ritual, worship the gods for the one who seeks the gods; as the joyous Hotṛ, you shine forth beyond all failures.
O Purifier, shine upon us with splendid and heroic strength;
be most intimate to those who praise you for our well-being.
The inspired poets, praising you and remaining vigilant, kindle you—
the immortal bearer of oblations, the increaser of strength.
Agni is the Hotṛ, the domestic priest of the sacrifice, the all-seeing; he knows the sacrifice in its proper sequence.
He, the immortal bearer of oblations, the eager messenger, well-disposed— Agni brings [the sacrifice] together through our prayer.
Agni, the ancient banner of sacrifice, takes notice through our prayer;
for his purpose is effective.
The gods have made Agni— the son of strength, the widely-renowned Jātavedas— their bearer.
Agni, the undeceivable leader of the human tribes,
is a swift chariot, ever new.
Overcoming all assailants, the unimpaired will-power of the gods— Agni is the one of most abundant renown.
Through his vehicle, the mortal who offers oblations attains the sacrificial foods and the dwelling of the one with purifying radiance.
May we, the inspired poets, through our hymns attain all the well-established [blessings] of Agni Jātavedas.
O Agni, may we win all desirable things in the contests for booty;
in you the gods have placed their power.
O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice through our songs, to the desirable cloud;
drink of this, impelled by our prayer.
O Indra and Agni, the conscious sacrifice goes forth together with the singer;
through this [hymn], drink this pressed [soma].
I choose Indra and Agni, who delight in the seers, with the impulse of the sacrifice;
may they both satisfy themselves here with the soma.
I invoke the two impetuous slayers of Vṛtra, the victorious and unconquered,
Indra and Agni, the greatest winners of booty.
The chanters, skilled in hymns and knowing the ways of song, sing forth to you both;
O Indra and Agni, I choose for myself strengthening food.
O Indra and Agni, with a single deed you simultaneously shook down the ninety forts belonging to the Dāsas.
O Indra and Agni, from the work of the waters, the inspired thoughts go forth along the paths of Truth.
O Indra and Agni, powerful are your abodes and your offerings; your crossing of the waters is established.
O Indra and Agni, you adorn the luminous realms of heaven for the sake of spoils;
that heroic deed of yours is well known.
I shall sing forth for you the highest hymn to this god Agni;
may he come to us with the gods, and as the best of sacrificers, may he sit upon the sacred grass.
He who is the observer of Truth, whose skill both heaven and earth attend, and whose aids are with him—
him the offerers of oblations invoke, seeking to win his protection.
He is the guide of these inspired singers; for he is indeed the master of the sacrifices.
Pay homage to that Agni of yours, who is the giver and the winner of wealth.
May that Agni grant us most peaceful protections for our enjoyment,
from which he may shower wealth upon us— upon those dwelling in heaven and those in the waters.
The chanters kindle Agni—the radiant, the peerless—with his excellent thoughts; he is the Hotṛ-priest, the lord of the people, the lord of the clans.
And may you, O Brahman, most invoked by the gods, protect us during our hymns;
O Agni, increased by the Maruts, shine auspiciously upon us as the greatest winner of thousands.
Now grant us, O Agni, wealth consisting of thousands, along with offspring and prosperity; grant us brilliant, heroic strength, most excellent and undecaying.
The joyous Hotṛ has taken his place at the assemblies; he is the true sacrificer, the most wise, the ordainer.
Agni, whose chariot is lightning, the son of strength, with flaming hair, has spread his brilliance over the earth.
I offer this word of homage to you; accept it, O observer of Truth, for you are mindful, O powerful one.
Knowing all, bring hither the wise ones and sit upon the sacred grass in their midst for our protection, O worshipful one.
May the two Dawns, seeking strength, hasten toward you, O Agni, along the paths of the wind;
when they anoint that ancient one with oblations, they stand in the dwelling like two riders upon a chariot-seat.
O powerful Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, and all the Maruts, sing your praise for the sake of bliss,
when you, O son of strength, stand with your flame over the dwellings, spreading out men like the sun.

Having approached you today with uplifted hands and with reverence, we have indeed fulfilled your desire. O Agni, as a sage, worship the gods with a most sacrificial mind and with an unfailing thought.
For from you, O Son of Strength, proceed many aids of the god, as well as prizes of victory.
Grant us thousandfold wealth, O Agni, according to your truthful word that is free from guile.
For you, O Dakṣa, of sage-like intellect, O God, we mortals have performed these rites at the sacrifice;
take note of every well-yoked chariot, and O immortal Agni, enjoy all that.
Flashing forth with your broad radiance, drive away our enemies, the demons, and diseases.
May I abide in the protection of the great Agni, who grants excellent refuge, under the guidance of him who is easily invoked.
Be our protector at the dawning of this very dawn, and be our guardian when the sun has risen.
O Agni, well-born in body, take pleasure in my hymn of praise, just as one enjoys his own constant offspring.
O Agni, you who behold men, as a bull shine forth in many directions, red amidst the dark ones.
O Vasu, lead us and carry us across distress; O youngest one, grant us wealth according to our desire.
O invincible Agni, shine forth as a bull, having conquered all strongholds for the sake of prosperity;
O Jātavedas, you are the leader of the foremost sacrifice, the protector, and the excellent guide of the great rite.
O singer, you who are wise and shining toward the gods, grant us many flawless shelters.
Like a prize-winning chariot, bring us strength, O Agni; may you establish for us the two well-established worlds, heaven and earth.
O Bull, cause us to swell and quicken our strengths; O Agni, make the two worlds yield milk for us.
O God, shining with a brilliant luster along with the gods, let not the ill-will of a mortal encompass us.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, full of wondrous power, and most enduring.
May there be to us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours be ours.
This Agni is the lord of great heroic power and of great good fortune;
he is the lord of wealth consisting of noble offspring and cattle, and he is the lord of the slaying of Vṛtra.
O Maruts, O heroes, attend upon this man who increases your strength, in whom there are auspicious riches;
those who overcome the wicked in battles have destroyed the enemy every day.
As such, O bounteous Agni, sharpen us for wealth consisting of excellent heroic power— O you of many glories, for that which is most exalted, rich in progeny, free from disease, and full of vigor.
He who has made all worlds his own, who has overcome them, and who has established worship among the gods—
he strives for the gods, for great heroic power, and for the praise of men.
O Agni, do not deliver us over to thoughtlessness, nor to lack of heroes, nor to lack of singers, O son of strength; nor to reproach. Drive away our enemies.
O fortunate Agni, grant us at this great sacrifice abundant strength accompanied by offspring;
O you of many glories, endow us with even greater wealth that brings delight and renown.
Being kindled according to the first ordinances, he, the possessor of all boons, is anointed with unguents;
Agni—flame-haired, clothed in ghee, the purifier, the excellent sacrificer—is prepared for the sacrifice of the gods.
Just as you, O Agni Jātavedas, being wise, performed the office of the Hotṛ for the earth and for heaven, so with this oblation do you worship the gods; like Manu, further this sacrifice today.
Three are your lifespans, O Jātavedas; three are your births from the dawns, O Agni.
With these, as the one who knows, sacrifice for the protection of the gods, and then become the source of well-being and security for the sacrificer.

Praising Agni, the beautifully radiant and fair to behold, we pay homage to you, O Jātavedas, who are worthy of worship. The gods have made you their messenger, their steward, and the bearer of oblations—the navel of immortality.
O Agni, whatever Hotṛ-priest was before you, more skilled in sacrifice, established from of old and bringing bliss through his own power—
according to his law, O wise one, perform the sacrifice for us, and then establish our rite for the feast of the gods.
O Agni, be well-disposed toward us when we approach you—like a friend to a friend, like a father who is kind.
For the dwellings of men are full of many deceivers; burn up the hostile powers that turn against us.
O Agni, burn up the enemies within; burn away the curse of the distant, stingy foe.
O Vasu, you who are observant, burn those who are mindless; let your ageless, tireless flames spread abroad.
Desiring [success], O Agni, with fuel and ghee I offer this oblation for speed and strength;
as much as I am able, praising with a sacred prayer, I offer this divine hymn for a hundredfold gain.
O Son of Strength, praised with your flame, bestow great vital power upon those who labor;
O Agni, grant wealth, peace, and well-being to the Viśvāmitras, for we have cleansed your body many times over.
Bestow wealth, O excellent winner of riches; for such you indeed become, O Agni, when fully kindled.
In the dwelling of the fortunate singer, you possess abundant wealth; with outstretched arms, you assume wondrous forms.
I choose Agni as the Hotṛ at the sacrificial feast—the skillful sage, all-knowing and infallible.
May he, the most excellent sacrificer, worship among the gods for us; may he win us gifts for wealth and strength.
O Agni, I send forth toward you the ladle filled with oblation, radiant, bestowing gifts, and dripping with ghee.
Moving clockwise and choosing the assembly of gods, he has established the sacrifice with bounties and treasures.

With a most vigorous mind, O Agni, protect us; grant us the gift of good offspring, O Giver! In the abundance of the wealth of the most heroic man, may we be the ones to offer excellent praise to you, the Vasu.
For many are the faces that the worshipful people have placed in you, O Agni, the god;
so, O youngest one, bring hither the assembly of the gods, for today you shall sacrifice to the divine host.
When the gods, seating you as the Hotṛ priest at the sacrificial meal for the sake of worship,
anointed you, O Agni— be thou our protector here, and bestow glorious renown upon our bodies.
The priest invokes Agni, Uṣas, the Aśvins, and Dadhikrā with hymns at the break of dawn.
May the gods, possessing excellent light, hear us; may they, being of one accord and longing for the sacrifice, listen.
O Agni, born of Truth, three are your strengths, three your stations, and three are your ancient tongues. Three also are your bodies beloved by the gods; with these, protect our songs without fail.
O Agni Jātavedas, many are your names, O self-dependent god of immortality.
And those many illusions of the masters of illusion, O all-impelling one whose kinship is sought, you have gathered together within yourself.
Agni is the leader of the divine peoples like Bhaga; he is the god who guards the seasons and upholds the cosmic order.
As the slayer of Vṛtra, the ancient one, the possessor of all wealth, may he carry the singer across all difficulties.
I invoke here Dadhikrā, Agni, and the goddess Uṣas; Bṛhaspati and the god Savitṛ; the Aśvins, Mitra and Varuṇa, and Bhaga; the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas.
Place this sacrifice of ours among the immortals; O Jātavedas, enjoy these oblations.
O Agni, O Hotṛ, sitting down as the first, partake of the drops of fat and clarified butter.
O Purifier, drops of fat mixed with ghee drip for thee;
according to thy own law, grant us the most excellent treasure for the feast of the gods.
For you, O Agni, the wise one, the drops of clarified butter flow;
O truthful one, you are kindled as the best of seers; be the protector of the sacrifice.
For you, O Agni, the powerful one who is free from want, the drops of fat and ghee drip down.
Praised by the seers, come with your lofty luster; O wise one, graciously accept the offerings.
The most powerful fat has been extracted from your midst; we offer it to you.
O Vasu, the drops drip upon your skin; accept them, O God, for each of the deities.
This is that Agni in whom Indra, longing for him, has placed the pressed Soma within his belly;
having won thousandfold booty like a swift steed, you are praised, O Jātavedas.

O Agni, that splendor of yours which is in heaven, on earth, in the plants, and in the waters, O worshipful one— by which you have spread across the wide mid-air— that light of yours is brilliant, surging, and beheld by men.
O Agni, you go toward the flood of heaven; you have called upon the gods who are worthy of worship.
You approach those waters which are in the luminous realm beyond the sun, and those which stand below it.
May the fires of the soil, in harmony with those of the flowing waters, being free from malice and disease, graciously accept this sacrifice and the great, abundant nourishments.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, wondrous and most enduring.
May there be to us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours be ours.
Rubbed forth and well-established in his dwelling, the youthful sage, the leader of the sacrifice—Agni, the ageless one among the aging woods; here Jātavedas has established immortality.
The two Bharatas, Devaśravas and Devavāta, have churned forth the wealthy Agni, the highly skillful one.
O Agni, look out for us with great wealth; be our leader through the days to come.
The ten fingers have generated him, the ancient one, well-born among his mothers and dear to them. Praise Agni, the son of Devavāta, O Devaśravas—he who shall become the master of men.

I have established you in the best place on earth, in the station of *iḷā*, in the auspiciousness of the days. O Agni, shine with wealth upon the *dṛṣadvatī*, at the human watering-place, and upon the *sarasvatī*.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḷā*—the gift of cattle, full of wondrous power, and most enduring.
May there be to us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, let that benevolence of yours be with us.
O Agni, overcome the hostile armies, casting away those who oppose us;
invincible, crossing over the enemies, bestow splendor upon the one who brings the sacrifice.
O Agni, you are kindled with the *iḷā* offering, the immortal invoker who is sought for the sacrifice; graciously accept our ritual service today.
O Agni, wakeful son of strength, invoked with oblations, come with your splendor to this sacred grass,
my seat.
O Agni, together with all the fires and the gods, magnify our songs—
those who are attentive at the sacrifices.
O Agni, grant wealth consisting of heroic sons to the donor; bestow upon us abundance and make us rich in offspring.
O Agni, you are the wise son of Heaven, and by your lineage you belong to Earth as well, you who possess all knowledge.
O conscious one, sacrifice here to the gods individually.
Agni, the wise one, wins heroic powers; he wins booty, adorning himself for immortality.
O you who abound in food, bring the gods here to us.
Agni, the unerring one, shines upon heaven and earth, the two immortal goddesses who belong to all people;
he dwells among them with strengths, most radiant through our homages.
O Agni and Indra, come here to the sacrifice in the house of the donor who has pressed the Soma;
O Gods, do not fail us, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Agni, son of strength, Jātavedas, you are kindled in the home of the waters as a constant one;
exalting with your aid, you honor the places of assembly.

Having perceived Agni Vaiśvānara with our minds, we, possessing oblations, praise him who is worthy of invocation, the finder of heaven—the bountiful god, the charioteer, the delightful one; seeking wealth, the Kuśikas call upon him with songs.

We invoke that bright Agni for protection—Vaiśvānara, Mātariśvan, the one worthy of praise; Bṛhaspati, the inspired singer who hears us for the sake of the gods’ service, the guest who hastens swiftly toward his goal.
Like a neighing horse, Vaiśvānara is kindled by the Kuśikas with their wives, age after age.
May that Agni, ever-watchful among the immortals, bestow upon us great heroism, abundance of horses, and treasure.
Let the Vājas go forth with their powers like fires; mingled for glory, they have yoked the spotted deer.
The Maruts, great in their growth and all-knowing, the invincible ones, cause the mountains to tremble.
The Maruts, adorned with fire, who belong to all people—we implore their fierce and mighty protection.
They, the sons of Rudra, resounding, clothed in rain, like lions in their impetuous intent, are bounteous givers.
We pray with excellent praises for troop after troop, for host after host: for the splendor of Agni and the might of the Maruts.
With spotted deer as their steeds, possessing inexhaustible wealth, they come to the sacrifice, wise ones at the assemblies.
I am Agni, by birth Jātavedas; clarified butter is my eye, and nectar is in my mouth. I am the threefold hymn, the measurer of the mid-region; I am the imperishable heat, my name is the oblation.
With three purifiers he cleansed the hymn, discerning with his heart the thought and the light;
by his own powers he fashioned the most excellent treasure and then beheld heaven and earth all around.

The inexhaustible fountain with a hundred streams, the wise father of all that is spoken; him who rejoices in the womb of his parents as a celebrant—O Heaven and Earth, fulfill him whose word is truth.
Forward for you go the strengths, seeking heaven, accompanied by oblations and the butter-spoon; they approach the gods, desiring their favor.
I praise with song Agni, the wise, the accomplisher of the sacrifice,
who is prompt to hear and who holds the offerings.
O Agni, may we be able to control the vigorous power of you, the god;
may we cross over all hostilities.
Being kindled at the sacrifice, Agni, the purifier worthy of praise,
whose hair is flame— him we implore.
Broad-chested, immortal, clothed in ghee, well-invoked with *svāhā*,
Agni is the carrier of oblations for the sacrifice.
Those who press on with the ladle uplifted, possessing the sacrifice and this very prayer,
have brought Agni hither for their protection.
The immortal god, the Hotṛ, goes before us with his creative power,
impelling the assemblies of knowledge.
The prize-winner is placed among the prizes; he is led forward at the sacrifices—the inspired singer who accomplishes the rite.
Worthy of choice, he was fashioned by wisdom; he received the germ of beings, the father of Dakṣa, through his own body.
I have established you, the most excellent one, O Agni, born of strength, through the praise of skillful power— the radiant and longing one.
The inspired singers kindle Agni with strengthening offerings— the leader, the one who crosses the waters, the one they seek at the harnessing of the sacred Law.
I praise Agni at the sacrifice— the Son of Strength, shining toward heaven, the one possessed of the wisdom of a seer.
Worthy of invocation and homage, visible even through the darkness,
Agni, the bull, is kindled.
Agni, the bull, is kindled like a horse that carries the gods;
him the offerers of oblations praise.
O bull, we who are bulls ourselves kindle you, the bull,
O Agni, as you shine forth mightily.
O Agni Jātavedas, accept our oblation, the sacrificial cake (puroḷāśa),
at the morning libation, O you who are enriched by prayer!
O Agni, this sacrificial cake has been cooked for you, or perhaps it has been fully prepared;
accept it with pleasure, O youngest one!
O Agni, partake of the sacrificial cake offered on the day before yesterday;
you, O Son of Strength, are established at this sacrifice.
O Jātavedas, O Sage, at the midday libation, enjoy the sacrificial cake here;
O Agni, the wise do not diminish your portion in the assemblies, for you are the mighty one.
O Agni, son of strength, take pleasure at the third libation in the offered sacrificial cake;
then, through inspired praise, establish among the immortal gods the wakeful sacrifice, rich in treasures.
O Agni, increasing one, O Jātavedas, graciously accept this oblation, the cake offered on the day before yesterday.
Here is this fire-drill; here is the means for producing [fire] that has been prepared. Bring hither this mistress of the people; let us churn Agni in the ancient manner.
Jātavedas has been deposited in the two fire-sticks, well-established like an embryo within pregnant women;
day by day Agni is to be praised by watchful men who bring oblations.
O wise one, bring [the oblation] down upon her who lies extended; she, having been impregnated, has immediately given birth to the bull.
With his ruddy crest and brilliant luster, the son of *Iḷā* has been born according to the sacred law.
In the place of Iḷā, upon the navel of the earth, O Jātavedas Agni, we establish you so that you may carry the oblation.
O men, churn forth the sage, the one without guile, the wise, the immortal with the beautiful countenance;
O men, bring forth Agni, the banner of sacrifice, the first in the east, the most gracious.
When they churn him with their arms, he shines forth like a prize-winning steed, ruddy among the woods;
brilliant on his course like that of the Aśvins, unrestrained, he sweeps past the stones, burning up the grass.
Born, Agni shines forth, observant, a prize-winner, a sage praised by seers, a bountiful giver—
him whom the gods established at the sacrifices as the one to be invoked, the all-knowing bearer of oblations.

Sit down, O Hotṛ, in your own place, being wise; establish the sacrifice in the womb of the well-performed rite. As one who pleases the gods, worship the gods with the oblation; O Agni, bestow great vitality upon the sacrificer.
Produce smoke, O friends, like a bull; go toward the prize without failing. This Agni is the conqueror of armies and possesses great heroes, by whom the gods overcame the Dasyus.
This is your seasonal birthplace, from which, once born, you shone forth;
knowing it, O Agni, sit down here, and then cause our songs of praise to flourish.
He is called Tanūnapāt when he is the embryo of the Asura; he becomes Narāśaṃsa when he is born.
When Mātariśvan measured out his form within the mother, he became the rush of the wind in his swift course.
Well-rubbed by vigorous rubbing, well-placed by skillful setting, O Agni, the sage; perform the rites well for the sacrifice and worship the gods for the one who seeks the gods.
Mortals have brought forth the immortal one—him who is unwearied, the crosser, with firm jaws.
The ten unwedded sisters, moving together, grasp him at birth as he becomes a man.
The seven-hotted one shone forth from of old when he blazed in his mother’s lap at her udder;
day after day the joyous one does not close his eyes, since he was born from the belly of the Asura.

Armed against enemies like the onset of the Maruts, these first-born of the sacred word (brahman) know all things. The Kuśikas have offered a glorious prayer; each one in his own home has kindled the fire.
Since we have chosen you here today, O wise Hotṛ, as this sacrifice proceeds;
since you have been firm and have performed your work with steadfastness, come to the Soma, knowing and discerning all.
The Soma-loving friends desire you; they press the Soma and present the sacrificial foods.
They endure the insults of men, for, O Indra, no wisdom whatsoever exists apart from you.
Not even the furthest regions are distant for you; come hither, O Lord of Bay Steeds, with your two bay horses!
These libations have been prepared for the steadfast Bull; the pressing-stones are set in motion as the fire is kindled.

Indra, fair-cheeked, bounteous, the overcomer, with his great host, mighty in action, and impetuous— when you, O fierce one, were established among mortals as a protector, where then, O bull, are those heroic deeds of yours?
For you alone, shaking even what is unshakable, go forth slaying the Vṛtras;
for your ordinance, heaven and earth and the mountains stand as if fixed in their places.
Moreover, O much-invoked one, in safety you alone, through your glories, have spoken firmly as the slayer of Vṛtra.
Even these two boundless worlds, O Indra, when you grasp them together, are but a handful to you, O Maghavan.
O Indra, let your two bay horses go forth down the slope; let your thunderbolt go forth, crushing the enemies.
Slay those who face you, those who follow behind, and those who flee away; make all truth prevail, and let it be spread abroad.
The mortal to whom you have granted sustenance shares even that which was not his portion, the household wealth;
O Indra, invoked by many, may your auspicious favor be dripping with clarity, and your gift consist of a thousandfold.
O Indra, much-invoked, you crushed Kuṇāru, who dwelt with Dānu and was handless;
O Indra, with your might, you struck down the footless Vṛtra as he grew arrogant and hostile.
O Indra, you have established in its seat the level, vigorous, great, and boundless earth; the Bull has propped up the sky and the mid-air; let the waters flow here, impelled by you.
O Indra, Vala, who had no enemy, opened the cow-pen out of fear before you struck;
he made the paths easy to travel so that the cows might emerge. The voices of praise, blowing forth, gave aid to the one invoked by many.
Alone, O Indra, you have filled the two world-halves joined together—the earth and the sky.
And from the mid-air, O Hero, as the charioteer of our battle, bring to us the yoked spoils and strengths.

The sun does not violate the directions assigned to him day after day, impelled by the one with bay horses; when he has traversed his paths, he then effects his release with his horses—this is his work.
They longed to behold the great, wondrous face of the radiant Dawn as she came from the night;
all recognize her when she has arrived in her majesty—the many well-performed deeds of Indra.
A great light is deposited within her flanks; the raw cow moves about bearing the cooked [milk].
Every sweetness is gathered within the cow, which Indra placed there for our nourishment.
O Indra, be firm; the snares have been set. Aid the sacrifice for the sake of the singer and his friends.
Let the mortals of evil designs and wicked intent, the armed enemies, be struck down.
The clamor is heard from the nearby enemies; strike them down with your most scorching thunderbolt!
Cut them off from below, shatter them, and overcome them! Slay the *rakṣas*, O Maghavan, and deliver them into our hands.
Uproot the *rakṣas* with its very root, O Indra; cut it in the middle and crush its tip.
How long have you delayed? Cast your burning weapon at the hater of prayer!
For our well-being, O Leader, when you sit down with the swift steeds at the many great refreshments, may we be winners of vast wealth;
O Indra, may there be for us a fortune accompanied by progeny.
O Indra, bring us resplendent fortune; may we take possession of the abundance of your gift.
Our desire has spread out like the ocean; O Lord of Wealth, fulfill it with riches.

Satisfy this desire with cattle and horses, and extend it with radiant wealth. Seeking the light of heaven, the wise Kuśikas have fashioned this hymn for you, O Indra, as an offering with their prayers.
O Lord of Cows, burst open the cow-pens for us; let gains and strengths come to us together.
You are the dweller in heaven, O Bull of true vigor; O Maghavan, be a good giver of cattle to us.
We invoke for our good fortune the bounteous Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty—
him who hears us, the fierce one for our protection in conflicts, the slayer of Vṛtras, and the winner of riches.
The wise bearer of oblations, instructing the granddaughter of his daughter and honoring the meditation of *ṛta*,
sped forth with a favorable mind to the outpouring of the father upon his daughter.
The kinsman has not left his inheritance to his sister; he made her a womb, a place for the winner’s treasure.
When the mothers generated the bearer, one was the maker of good deeds, the other the one who cried out.
Agni was born, trembling with his tongue, as the sons of the Great One were presented before the ruddy one.
Great is the embryo; great is their birth; great is the growth of the one with bay horses through the sacrifices.
Victorious songs attended him; they recognized the great light emerging from the darkness.
Knowing him, the dawns rose up toward him; Indra alone became the lord of the cattle.
The wise ones, the seven sages, with their minds directed forward, pierced through the firm obstacles;
they discovered the entire path of *ṛta*, and knowing it, he entered therein with reverence.
When Saramā found the breach of the mountain, she made the great, ancient path converge;
the swift-footed one led the way at the head of the flowing streams, and knowing well, she went first toward the roar.

The wisest one came, seeking friendship; the mountain brought forth the germ for the pious man. The youth, eager for the sacrifice, won with his companions; then he instantly became an Aṅgiras, singing his praise.
The manifest presence before us, the counterpart of every being, knows all generations and slays Śuṣṇa.
May he, the path-finder from heaven, seeking cattle and singing our praise, as a friend release his friends from reproach.

With minds longing for cattle, they sat down with hymns, preparing a path toward immortality. This indeed is their abundant dwelling place, by which they sought to win the months through the Eternal Law (*ṛta*).
Beholding their own milk, they rejoiced while milking the seed of the ancient;
their roar heated heaven and earth, and when [the cattle] were born, they established the heroes among the kine.
He, the slayer of Vṛtra, with his progeny and with oblations, with hymns, released the cows;
for him, the widely-striding noble cow, yielding ghee, milked out the sweet, delicious honey.

For his sake, the skillful ones prepared a seat; they indeed beheld his great, radiant splendor. With a supporting pillar they steadied the two parents; sitting there, they erected the impetuous one on high.
When the great Dhiṣaṇā impelled him who grows instantly and pervades both worlds,
in whom all blameless songs are united— all invincible powers for Indra.
I desire your friendship and your powers; many teams go forth to the slayer of Vṛtra.
We have come with a great hymn of praise to the patron; O Maghavan, be our good protector.
Having found the great, widely-shining domain, Indra then brought forth a path for his friends;
shining with the men, he brought forth at once the sun, the dawn, the way, and Agni.
Even the waters, the far-reaching mistress of the house, he has released flowing together, all-glittering;
being purified by the poets with their filters, they flow through the days and nights, sweetening the honeyed draughts.
The two dark treasuries of wealth follow after thee, O worshipful Sūrya, through thy greatness,
when thy friends, O Indra, eager for the desirable prize, strive to encompass thy majesty with their straight-flying arrows.

Become the lord of our true blessings, O slayer of Vṛtra; you are the life-sustaining bull of all songs, bestowing vital strength. Come to us with your auspicious friendships, great one, hastening with your mighty aids.
Worshipping him with reverence as did Aṅgiras, I fashion this new hymn for you, O Ancient One.
Drive away the many godless deceivers; and grant us our own wealth, O Maghavan, so that we may win it.
The purifying mists have spread far and wide; carry us safely to the further shore of them.
O Indra, you who are the charioteer, protect us from harm; very swiftly, make us winners of cattle.
The slayer of Vṛtra, the lord of cattle, has bestowed the cows; with his ruddy abodes he has passed through the black one.
Indicating the direction by means of truth, he has thrown open all his own doors.
We invoke the auspicious Maghavan Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty;
the fierce one who hears us, for our protection in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras and is the winner of riches.
O Indra, Lord of Soma, drink this Soma, this midday libation which is dear to you. Puffing out your cheeks, O Maghavan, O consumer of the dregs, unyoke your two bay horses here and rejoice.
O Indra, drink the Soma mixed with milk and curds, the stirred offering, the bright juice; we have given it to you for exhilaration.
Being of one mind with the host of Maruts who perform sacred prayer, together with the Rudras, pour down the rain in abundance.
O Indra, those Maruts who increased your breath, your power, and your strength while singing praise—
O wielder of the thunderbolt, O fair-cheeked one, drink at the midday libation together with the troop of Rudras.
The Maruts who were there, that vigorous host of Indra—verily they, the inspired ones, have now proclaimed his sweetness;
by them, when impelled, he found the vital spot of Vṛtra, who considered himself invulnerable.

O Indra, enjoying the libation like Manu, drink the Soma for eternal heroic power. O Lord of the Bay Horses, turn hither through our sacrifices; with your swift steeds, you set the floods of water flowing.
When you, O Indra, having slain Vṛtra, released the waters so that they might flow like racing mares,
you struck down with your moving weapon the godless one who lay encompassing the goddesses.
Let us worship with homage Indra, the exalted, the vast, the towering, the ageless, the youthful— he, the worthy of sacrifice,
whose greatness the two beloved worlds have not measured, nor do they encompass his majesty.
The many well-performed deeds of Indra—none of all the gods transgress his ordinances.
He who supported this earth and yonder heaven, the one of wondrous power who begot the sun and the dawn.
O guileless one, this is your true greatness: that as soon as you were born, you drank the Soma.
O Indra, neither the days nor the nights, nor the months, nor the autumns can restrain the power of you who are so mighty.
As soon as you were born, O Indra, you drank the Soma for exhilaration in the highest heaven;
when you entered Heaven and Earth, you then became the ancient sustainer of the poets.
You slew the serpent as he lay encompassing the waters, O many-born one, you who are stronger than the one displaying his might.
Even the sky did not equal your greatness when, with one hip, you took up the earth.

For the sacrifice, O Indra, has been your strengthener; it is dear to you, the pressed Soma and the sacrificial food. Being worthy of worship, protect sacrifice with sacrifice; the sacrifice aided your thunderbolt in the slaying of the serpent.

With sacrifice and for aid, I have brought Indra hither; may I turn him toward us for newest favor—he who has grown great through ancient hymns, through those of the middle age, and through the most recent.
Since the inspired thought has entered me and brought me forth, I shall praise Indra before the decisive day,
so that he may carry us across from distress— him whom both sides invoke as he goes like a ship.
His beaker is full; Svāhā! Like a pourer, I have filled the vessel for him to drink.
The dear Soma drops have turned together toward Indra for his exhilaration, moving in a clockwise direction.
Neither the deep-flowing Sindhu nor the mountains surrounding you have held you back, O much-invoked Indra, when thus impelled by your friends, you shattered even the firm enclosure of cattle.
We invoke the auspicious Maghavan Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty;
the fierce one who hears us, for our protection in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras and is the winner of riches.
From the lap of the mountains, longing [to flow], like two mares let loose, vying with one another;
like two bright mother-cows licking [their calves], the Vipāś and Śutudrī rush forth with their waters.
Impelled by Indra, seeking his impulse, you two go toward the ocean like two charioteers; meeting together, swelling with your waves, O radiant ones, one of you flows into the other.
I have come toward the most motherly river; we have reached the broad and auspicious Vipāś.
Like two mothers licking their calf, they move together, following their common source.
Swelling with this milk, we move along the god-fashioned womb; our impetus is set in motion so that it cannot be turned back—what does the inspired singer desire as he calls aloud to the rivers?

O you who follow the cosmic order (*ṛtāvarī*), rest for a moment according to your ways at my Soma-offering word! Seeking aid, the son of Kuśika has called forth the great Sindhu with this inspired thought (*manīṣā*).
Indra, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, has dug us out; he struck down Vṛtra, the dam of the rivers.
The god Savitṛ, the fair-handed, has led us forth; by his impulse we go across the wide expanses.
That heroic deed of Indra’s must be proclaimed forever: how he tore the dragon asunder;
with his thunderbolt he struck down those who sat around him, while the waters went forth, seeking their course.
O singer, do not forget these words, even as later generations raise their voices for you; O bard, be well-pleased with our hymns, do not cast us down among men—homage be to you!
O sisters, listen well to the singer; he has come to you from afar with wagon and chariot. Bow down low; become easy to cross, O rivers, flowing downward with your currents below the axle.
O *kārū*, let us hear your words as you have come from afar with wagon and chariot.
I bow down before you like a swelling woman; like a maiden to a young man, I am ever devoted to you.

O Aṅga, when the Bharatas, seeking cattle, shall cross over you—impelled by the people and urged on by Indra—then let the impulse flow forth, speeding in its course; I choose for myself the favor of you who are worthy of sacrifice.
The Bharatas, seeking cattle, have crossed over; the sage has obtained the favor of the rivers.
Swell forth, you who provide nourishment and great wealth; fill your channels and flow swiftly!
May your wave, O waters, strike against the yoke-pin; release the thongs.
Let the two inviolable cows, though they have committed no offense and are free from guilt, swell with milk.
Indra, the breaker of forts, struck down the Dāsa with his hymns; finding wealth and showing mercy, he scattered his enemies.
Urged by prayer and increasing in body, the giver of much filled both heaven and earth.
I send forth my speech, adorning it for the sake of immortality, to stir the impulse of you, the powerful Makha.
O Indra, you are the first leader of the human settlements and of the divine tribes as well.
Indra, whose aim is to destroy, overthrew Vṛtra; he, whose aim is to transform, frustrated the wiles of the guileful.
He slew Vyansa, burning fiercely among the woods, and made manifest the lowing of the cows of the nights.

Indra, winner of the light, generating the days, has conquered the hostile armies with his helpers, being the one who overcomes. He made the banner of the days shine for Manu; he found the light for the great battle.
Indra has entered into his impetuous strength with power, bestowing many manly deeds like a hero; for he has inspired these prayers for the singer and has heightened this bright color of theirs.
They celebrate the many great deeds well-performed by this great Indra:
with his host he crushed the crooked ones; with his wondrous powers, he of surpassing might, overcame the Dasyus.

In battle, Indra by his greatness created wide space for the gods; he, the true lord, the filler of the people, dwells in the seat of Vivasvat. These deeds of his the inspired singers and sages praise with hymns.
Satrāsāha, the most excellent, the giver of strength, who won the light of heaven and the divine waters—
he who conquered both the earth and this sky, after him the wise ones rejoice with hymns of praise.
Indra won the steeds and he won the sun; Indra won the cow that provides much nourishment.
He won golden wealth as well; having slain the Dasyus, he protected the Aryan race.
Indra won the plants and the days; he won the forest trees and the mid-air.
He split Vala and drove away the contending voices; thus he became the tamer of those who act with hostile intent.
We invoke the auspicious Maghavan Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty;
the one who hears us, the fierce one for our protection in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras and wins riches.
Mount the two bay steeds yoked to your chariot; come toward us like Vāyu with his teams.
Drink the soma juice, O Indra, being poured forth among us; Svāhā! We have offered it to you for your exhilaration.
I yoke the two swift, bay steeds to the pole of the chariot for the one invoked by many,
so that they may rush hither from every side and bring Indra to this well-prepared sacrifice.
Bring hither the two bulls, O burner; come down here, O self-dependent bull!
Let the two horses devour; unyoke here the two ruddy steeds. Day by day eat the roasted grains that are alike.
With a sacred prayer, I yoke for you the two swift bay steeds, companions joined by prayer, who revel together;
mounting your firm and comfortable chariot, O Indra, come to the Soma as one who is wise and discerning.
Let not other sacrificers detain your two vigorous, smooth-backed bay steeds.
Pass by all others; we shall be ready for you with the pressed Soma juices.
This Soma is for you; come hither! Being well-disposed, drink of it most constantly. Sitting down upon the sacrificial grass at this sacrifice, O Indra, take this drop into your belly.
The sacred grass is strewn for you; O Indra, the Soma is pressed, and the parched grains are prepared for your two bay steeds to eat.
To you, who dwell there, the many-powerful bull accompanied by the Maruts—to you, these oblations are offered.
O Indra, the men, the mountains, and the waters have made this [soma] sweet with milk for you.
Having come to it, O exalted one, drink it with a gracious mind; knowing and wise, follow your own paths.
O Maruts, those whom you shared in the Soma, who strengthened you and became your host— O Indra,
being of one mind with them and longing for it, drink this Soma with the tongue of Agni.
O Indra, drink of the pressed juice according to your own nature, or drink with the tongue of Agni, O worshipful one;
O Śakra, enjoy the sacrifice offered from the hand of the *adhvaryu* or that of the *hotṛ*, and take pleasure in the oblation.
We invoke for our good fortune the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty—
the fierce one who hears us, who comes to our aid in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras, and who wins riches.
Place this offering before us for our gain, O Indra, who are ever approaching with your aids;
you who have grown great at every libation through your own increasing powers, and who have become renowned through your mighty deeds.
For Indra, the Soma juices have been known since ancient times—those by which he became the skillful R̥bhu, vast and strong-jointed.
Welcome these as they are being offered; O Indra, drink of the bull, the one shaken by the strong ones.

Drink and grow strong; for yours indeed are the pressed Soma-draughts, O Indra—both those of old and these here now. Just as you drank the ancient Somas, O Indra, so drink them today, O Wondrous One, as one who is newer.
A great vessel, overflowing in the assembly, he possesses fierce might and daring strength;
even the earth could not contain him when the Soma juices exhilarated the Lord of the Bay Steeds.

Great and fierce, he has grown for heroic power; the bull has gathered himself through poetic wisdom. Indra is the giver of fortune; his cows bestow booty, and his many sacrificial gifts are born forth.
When the rivers went forth according to their impulse, as waters flow to the ocean like charioteers on their way,
Indra is even vaster than that seat when the Soma, the pressed stalk, fills him.
Like rivers flowing toward the ocean, bringing well-pressed Soma for Indra, they—skilled with their hands—milk the stalk with their arms; they purify the honey with a stream through the filters.
Like lakes are his bellies that hold the Soma; he has encompassed many libations. When Indra had consumed the first foods and slain Vṛtra, he chose the Soma.
Bring it hither; let no one stand in the way of this, for we know you to be the lord of riches.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Horses, bestow upon us that magnificent gift which is yours.
O Indra, Maghavan, wielder of the *ṛjīṣa*, bestow upon us wealth that is abundant and possesses every desirable thing.
Grant us a hundred autumns to live, and grant us, O fair-cheeked Indra, perpetual heroic sons.
We invoke for our good fortune the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty;
the fierce one who listens, who comes to our aid in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras, and who wins riches.
O Indra, we turn you toward us for the slaying of Vṛtra, for strength, and for victory in battle.
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, may the priests bring your mind and your eye hitherward toward us.
O Śatakratu, we invoke all your names with every song for the sake of overcoming our adversaries,
O Indra.
With the hundred powers of Puruṣṭuta, we magnify Indra, the sustainer of the people.
I invoke Indra, who is invoked by many, for the slaying of Vṛtra,
and for the winning of booty in battles.
Be victorious in the contests for booty; we implore you, O Śatakratu, O Indra, for the slaying of Vṛtra.
O Indra, be victorious in the contests for glory, in the battles for supremacy, in the raids for booty, and in the struggles against those who seek to overcome us.
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, drink for our protection the most vigorous, brilliant, and watchful Soma.
O Śatakratu, those senses of yours which are among the five peoples— O Indra, those I choose for you.
O Indra, great renown has come to you; bestow upon us invincible splendor. We cause your vital strength to swell upward.
Come to us from nearby, O Śakra, and also from afar;
O wielder of the thunderbolt, come here from whatever world is yours, O Indra.
Like a carpenter, I have fashioned this inspired thought with my intellect; like a prize-winning steed with a good yoke, I hasten along.
Touching upon my dearest and most distant goals, I, the wise one, desire to behold the seers.
Ask about the origin of the sages from the horse; supported by their minds, they fashioned the sky through their good deeds.
These prayers of thine, increasing and impelled by the mind, have now come into being according to the sacred law.

Placing secret things here, they anointed the two worlds for dominion; they measured them out with their measures and extended the two wide ones. The two great ones, meeting together, were established for nourishment within.
As he ascended, all gathered around him; clothed in splendors, he moves with self-luminous radiance.
Great is that name of the bull-like Asura; assuming every form, he has taken his stand upon the immortal realms.
The elder Bull begot these many powers of his;
O two Kings, sons of Heaven, through the prayers of the assembly, you have held sovereign power from days of old.
O two kings, you attend to the three many assemblies and all the seats at every time.
There, having gone in spirit, I beheld the Gandharvas with wind-like hair within the sacred law.
Now indeed, by means of the names of this bull and the cow, they have measured out the kinship of the bull;
clothing themselves in various divine forms, the masters of illusion have fashioned their appearance within him.
Now indeed, no one has surpassed this golden splendor which Savitṛ has extended for me.
With fair praise, he has encompassed the two world-halves that pervade all things; like a maiden, he has veiled his progeny.
You two accomplish the great ancient [work]; may you both be our divine protection on every side. All the wise ones behold the manifold deeds of the one who stands with tongue like a cowherd.
We invoke for our good fortune the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the winning of booty—
the mighty one who hears us, who comes to our aid in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras, and who is the conqueror of riches.
The prayer, fashioned into a hymn of praise, goes forth from the heart toward Indra as its lord;
it is vigilant when recited at the sacrifice. O Indra, know that which is born for you.
Born from heaven itself, ancient, wide-awake, and being recited at the sacrifice—
clothed in auspicious, bright garments, may this ancestral prayer of ours be established among us.
Even Yama’s mother has given birth here to twin sons; for the tip of the tongue has come forth flying.
These two, born as a pair, possess wondrous forms; they move together, dispelling darkness, at the base of the heat.
Among mortals, there is no one who can revile these, our fathers who were warriors for the sake of cattle.
Indra, the majestic and wondrous one, has made firm their strength and released the enclosures of the cows.
Where the friend, together with his friends, the Navagvas, went forth against the cattle with the warriors,
there Indra, with the ten Daśagvas, truly found the sun dwelling in the darkness.
Indra found the honey gathered in the cow, hoofed and hoofed, within the footprint of the bull;
hidden, secret, and concealed in the waters, he, the possessor of skill, took it in his right hand.
Discerning the light from the darkness, may we choose it; may we be far removed from misfortune in the encounter.
O Indra, drinker of Soma, increased by Soma, take pleasure in these songs of the most frequent singer.
May light follow the two worlds for the sake of the sacrifice; may we be far removed from great misfortune.
For even the many [enemies] of the impetuous mortal are overcome by the Vasus, who are easy to cross over and full of power.
We invoke for our good fortune the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty—
the mighty one who hears us, who comes to our aid in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras, and who is the winner of riches.
O Indra, we invoke you, the bull, when the Soma is pressed;
as such, drink of the sweet food.
O Indra, much-praised one, take pleasure in this pressed Soma that finds the power of the mind;
drink and pour it down until you are fully satisfied.
O Indra, praised one, Lord of the people, further our sacrifice accompanied by devotion along with all the gods.
O Indra, lord of the virtuous, these pressed Soma drops go forth to you; the bright drops seek your dwelling.
O Indra, take into your belly the pressed Soma, the most excellent;
your drops are celestial.
O lover of songs, drink our pressed juice; you are anointed with streams of honey.
O Indra, glory is indeed bestowed by you alone.
The imperishable splendors of the trees attend upon Indra;
having drunk of the Soma, he has grown strong.
Come to us from nearby and from afar, O slayer of Vṛtra;
take pleasure in these our songs.
When you are invoked between the far distance and the near,
O Indra, come here from there.
Come then to us, O Indra, being invoked toward me for the drinking of the Soma;
come with your two bay horses, O wielder of the stone.
The seasonal Hotṛ priest has sat down; the sacrificial grass has been spread in due order;
the pressing-stones have been yoked at dawn.
These prayers are being offered, O you who are borne by prayer; sit upon the sacred grass.
O Hero, partake of the sacrificial cake.
Rejoice in these libations of ours, O slayer of Vṛtra, in these hymns, O Indra, lover of songs, amidst our recitations!
Our thoughts lick the wide one who drinks the Soma, the Lord of Strength,
Indra, as mother cows lick their calf.
Do you, therefore, rejoice in this soma-juice for the sake of great bounty from your own body;
do not deliver your worshipper to reproach.
O Indra, we, seeking you and bearing oblations, sing your praises;
and you, O Vasu, are well-disposed toward us.
O Māra, release us from this; come hither, O lover of bay horses! O Indra, self-sustained one, rejoice here.
O Indra, may the two long-maned horses, dripping with clarity, carry you hither on a comfortable chariot to sit upon the sacred grass.
Come to our pressed Soma, O Indra, which is mixed with milk;
come with your two bay steeds, you who are well-disposed toward us.
O Indra, come to this exhilarating drink pressed by the stones upon the sacrificial grass; will you not indeed satisfy yourself with it?
Thus my songs have gone forth from here toward Indra, sent forth to turn him hither for the drinking of the Soma.
We invoke Indra here with hymns for the drinking of the Soma; will he not surely come through our songs of praise?
O Indra, these Soma juices have been pressed; take them into your belly, O Śatakratu, O possessor of wealth and horses!
For we know you, O Sage, as the winner of wealth, bold in battles;
therefore, we seek your favor.
O Indra, come with your bulls and drink this pressed juice of ours, mixed with milk and mixed with barley.
For you alone, O Indra, in your own dwelling, I urge the Soma for your drinking;
may this [Soma] delight in your heart.
We Kuśikas, seeking your aid, invoke you, O Indra, the ancient one, for the drinking of the pressed soma.
Come hither, standing upon the chariot-seat; to you belongs the drinking of Soma from days of old.
Unyoke your dear companions; these bearers of oblations call you to the sacred grass.
Come hither, passing over many peoples and the prayers of the enemy, with your two bay horses to us;
for these hymns, fashioned by praise, call upon you, O Indra, as they delight in your friendship.
O God Indra, come quickly with your bay horses to our sacrifice which increases through homage;
for I invoke you repeatedly with my prayers, offering oblations of clarified butter at the shared feast of the sweet draughts.
And may these two vigorous bay steeds, your companions, well-yoked and fair-limbed, bring you hither.
May Indra, enjoying the libation with parched grain, as a friend hear the praises of his friend.

Will you not make me the guardian of the people? Will you not make me the king, O Maghavan, O drinker of the dregs? Will you not make me a seer who has drunk of the pressed juice? Will you not grant me of the immortal wealth?
O Indra, let the great bay horses, harnessed for the feast, bring you hither;
they who from of old reach to the heights of heaven, well-groomed and eager for the bull.
O Indra, drink of the bull-strong juice shaken by the bull-strong [pressers], which the falcon brought for you who desired it;
in whose exhilaration you cause the peoples to tremble, and in whose exhilaration you threw open the cow-pens.
We invoke for our good fortune the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty;
