the fierce one who hears us, who comes to our aid in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras, and who is the winner of riches.
May this beloved Soma, pressed by the tawny steeds, be yours;
O Indra, being pleased with the tawny steeds, come to us and mount your tawny chariot.
Desiring the Dawn, you caused her to shine; desiring the Sun, you caused him to glow.
O Indra, possessor of bay horses, wise and discerning, you increase toward all glories.

Indra, the possessor of bay horses, has supported the heaven that nourishes the bay horses and the earth that is the form of the bay horses; with his bay horses he has established abundant food between those two, wherein the bay one moves.
Born as a tawny bull, he illumines the entire radiant realm;
the one with bay horses takes up his tawny weapon, the golden thunderbolt, within his arms.
Indra, with his bay horses, opened the way for the beloved, bright, and pure thunderbolt enveloped in light;
he drew forth the pressed juice with his bay steeds and brought the cows out with his bay steeds.
Come, O Indra, with your delightful bay horses whose hair is like peacock feathers;
let no one hold you back, as fowlers catch a bird—pass them by like a desert.
The devourer of Vṛtra, the breaker of Vala, the destroyer of fortresses, the progenitor of the waters;
Indra, the driver of the two bay steeds and the master of the chariot, shatters even that which is firm.
Like deep oceans, you nourish your mental power;
like cows, O good guardian, they have rushed forth toward the pasture as milch-cows reach a pool or streams flow into a lake.
Bring us powerful wealth, as one brings a share to those who acknowledge it; O Indra, shake down for us enduring riches, like ripe fruit from a tree with a hook.
O Indra, you are long-lived, self-ruling, of uniform command, and most glorious in your own renown. Increasing in might, O much-praised one, become for us the possessor of the greatest fame.

O Indra, renowned and great, the heroic deeds of you— the warrior, the bull, the self-ruling king, the fierce, the youthful, the ancient, the impetuous, and the undecaying wielder of the thunderbolt— are truly mighty.
Great art thou, O Mighty One, by thy manly powers, a seeker of wealth, O fierce one, overcoming others;
sole king of the entire world, do thou fight and cause the people to dwell in peace.
Shining forth, he has surpassed all measures; unassailed from every side, Indra has surpassed the gods.
By his might, Indra has surpassed heaven and earth, and the vast, wide mid-air, he who drinks the soma dregs.
The Soma juices, pressed from of old, enter into Indra— who is wide, deep, formidable by birth, all-encompassing, and the protector of prayers— just as rivers flow into the ocean.

O Indra, that Soma which Earth and Heaven bear for you out of love for you, as a mother bears her child—that very one they urge forward for you; the Adhvaryu priests cleanse it for you, O Bull, so that you may drink.
O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, as a bull for the battle, drink the Soma according to your custom for exhilaration.
Pour into your belly a wave of the sweet juice; you have been the king of the pressed libations from of old.
O Indra, being of one mind with the Maruts and accompanied by your host, drink the Soma, O wise hero, slayer of Vṛtra!
Slay our enemies, drive away those who assail us, and then grant us security from every side.
And according to the seasons, O guardian of the seasons, drink our pressed soma, Indra, together with the gods who are your friends.
The Maruts, whom you shared with, who followed you when you struck Vṛtra, have bestowed their power upon you.
O Maghavan, those who strengthened you at the slaying of Ahi, those at the battle with Śambara, O Lord of Bay Steeds, those at the quest for cattle,
and those sages who now rejoice after you— drink the Soma, O Indra, together with your host of Maruts.
We invoke here for new protection that Indra, the bull accompanied by the Maruts, who has grown great, the one without enemies, the divine ruler, the all-conquering, the fierce giver of victory.
As soon as he was born, the youthful bull desired to partake of the pressed juice;
drink of the pure draught according to your desire, for this is the first portion of the Soma mixed with milk for you.
On the day you were born, out of desire for this [Soma], you drank the mountain-dwelling nectar of the *aṃśu* stalk.
Your mother, the youthful woman who gave you birth, first poured that [nectar] for you into the house of the great father.
Having approached his mother, he sought food; he beheld the sharp Soma as his udder. Driving away the others, the skillful one moved forward; he of many forms performed great deeds.
Fierce, subduing the swift, possessing overwhelming power, he fashioned his body according to his will;
Indra, having overcome Tvaṣṭṛ by his very birth, drank the Soma from the vessels of that [demon].
We invoke the auspicious Indra, the bounteous lord, most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty;
the fierce one who listens, who comes to our aid in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras, and who is the winner of riches.
Praise the great Indra, in whom all the people who drink Soma have fulfilled their desire;
him, the one of excellent wisdom, fashioned by the two world-halves (Dhiṣaṇās), whom the gods generated as the shatterer of Vṛtras.

Whom indeed no one overcomes in battles—the self-ruling, most heroic one who stands upon his bay horses; he, the most powerful with his vigorous warriors, has shortened the life of the Dasyu with his wide-reaching strides.
Victorious in battles, a steed that crosses over, he has pervaded both heaven and earth, the bountiful one.
Like Bhaga to be invoked in the rite, he is dear to our hymns; like a father, he is gracious, easy to call upon, and the bestower of vital strength.
The upholder of heaven, the back of the mid-region, standing aloft like Vāyu’s chariot with its teams of horses and the Vasus;
the illuminator of nights, the progenitor of the sun, who distributes the portion like Dhiṣaṇā, as if for booty.
We invoke the auspicious Maghavan Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty;
the fierce one who listens, for our protection in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras and is the winner of riches.

May Indra drink with *svāhā*, he for whom the Soma is intended—having come as the fierce bull accompanied by the Maruts. May the wide-extending one be filled with these foods; may the oblation fulfill the desire of his body.
I yoke for you your two attendants for speed, whose obedience you have favored since days of old.
Here let your bay horses place you, O fair-cheeked one; drink of this well-pressed, delightful soma.
The singers have established Indra—the one who mingles with the cows and brings a successful crossing—for the sake of preeminence and sustenance.
O drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, rejoicing after drinking the Soma, impel cattle toward us in many ways.

Satisfy this desire with cattle and horses, and extend it with moon-bright bounty. Seeking the light of heaven, the wise Kuśikas have fashioned this hymn for you, O Indra, as a vehicle for your praise.
We invoke for our good fortune the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty;
the fierce one who hears us, for our protection in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras and is the winner of riches.
The lofty hymns have resounded toward Indra, the sustainer of the people, the bounteous one worthy of praise—
the immortal, much-invoked, who grows strong through well-fashioned songs and is celebrated day by day.
From every side, my songs go forth to Indra—the lord of a hundred powers, the ocean-like, the mighty hero;
the winner of booty, the breaker of forts, the swift one who crosses the waters, who dwells with his own power, the overcomer, and the finder of light.
In the mine of wealth, the singer is praised; Indra honors the unerring hymns of those who laud him.
For he has taken delight in the dwelling of Vivasvat; praise him, the ever-conquering slayer of the arrogant foe.

Sing forth with songs and hymns to you, the most heroic among men, O Hero, with persistent zeal! To you of many wondrous powers, he bows down for the sake of conquest; homage is his, for from of old he alone is the Lord.
Numerous are his invitations among mortals; the earth bears many riches for him.
For Indra, the heavens, the plants, and the waters guard their wealth—the living forests and the streams.
For you, O Indra, Lord of Bay Steeds, the sacred prayers and songs have been offered together; accept them with favor.
Be mindful as a kinsman for our newest aid; O Vasu, Friend, bestow vital strength upon those who sing your praise.
O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here, just as you drank of the pressed juice at Śāryāta’s sacrifice.
Under your guidance and in your protection, O Hero, the sages who perform fair sacrifices seek to win your favor.
Longing for it, O Indra, drink here our pressed soma with the Maruts as your companions,
since all the gods, O much-invoked one, surrounded you at your birth for the great battle.
In the crossing of the waters, O Maruts, he is our kinsman; they, bestowing excellent gifts, have gladdened Indra.
Together with them, let the slayer of Vṛtra drink the pressed Soma in the sacrificer’s own dwelling-place.
For this [Soma] has been pressed here with power, O Lord of bounties;
drink of it, O lover of songs.
O Soma, let him who follows your self-sustaining power restrain his body within the pressed juice;
may he, being worthy of Soma, exhilarate you.
May it reach your two flanks; O Indra, may it reach your head through this prayer; O Hero, extend your arms for the sake of bestowing wealth.
O Indra, at dawn, enjoy our offering accompanied by parched grains, by groats, by cakes, and by hymns of praise.
O Indra, enjoy this cooked sacrificial cake and give it your approval;
for you the oblations flow forth.
Eat our sacrificial cake and take pleasure in our songs,
as one desiring a bride approaches a young woman.
O you who are renowned from of old, enjoy our sacrificial cake at our morning libation;
for, O Indra, your power is indeed great.
O Indra, enjoy here at the midday pressing the parched grains and the lovely sacrificial cake,
while the praiser and singer, hastening toward his goal and acting like a bull, invokes you with his songs.
At the third libation, O much-praised one, grant us the parched grains and the offered sacrificial cake.
O Sage, may we, providing nourishment, serve you—who are accompanied by the *Ṛbhus* and possessed of vigor—with our prayers.

For you who are accompanied by Pūṣan, we have prepared the groats; for you who possess bay horses and are borne by bay steeds, we have prepared the parched grains. Eat the cake with your troop of Maruts; drink the Soma, O hero, slayer of Vṛtra, you who are wise.
Bring forth quickly for him roasted grains and the sacrificial cake for the most heroic of men.
Day after day, O Indra, may these similar offerings increase you for the drinking of Soma, O bold one!
O Indra and Parvata, bring hither on your lofty chariot desirable refreshments accompanied by noble heroes.
O Gods, enjoy the oblations at the sacrifices; wax strong, rejoicing in the hymns and the *iḷā* offering.
Stay here, O Maghavan; do not go away! Now I shall worship you with well-pressed Soma.
O Indra, O Lord of Power, like a son grasping his father’s hem, I take hold of your garment with a most sweet song.
Recite, O Adhvaryu; respond to me! Let us both prepare an acceptable offering for Indra.
Sit upon this sacrificial grass of the patron; then let the hymn be recited for Indra.
May he bring you home, O Maghavan; for that indeed is your place of origin. Let your harnessed bay steeds carry you thither.
Whenever we shall press the Soma, Agni shall speed as your messenger toward you.
Depart, O Maghavan, and come back again; O Indra, brother, your purpose lies in both places:
where the great chariot is stationed and where the prize-winning donkey is unyoked.
O Indra, you have drunk the Soma; go home. Your wife is beautiful, and your house is a place of joy.
Therein is the stationing of your great chariot, the unyoking of your vigorous steed, and the sacrificial fee.
These Bhojas, the Aṅgirases, the Virūpas— sons of Dyaus, heroes of the Asura—
granting riches to Viśvāmitra at the thousandfold pressing, have prolonged his life.
Maghavan assumes form after form, creating his own bodies through his powers of illusion;
when he comes from heaven three times in an instant, he, the observer of the cosmic order, drinks not according to the seasons but by his own sacred formulas.
The great seer, born of the gods and impelled by the gods, the beholder of men, propped up the billowy ocean;
when Viśvāmitra brought Sudās [across], Indra took pleasure in the Kuśikas.
Like swans, produce a hymn with the pressing-stones, rejoicing with songs at the sacrifice when the Soma is pressed;
together with the gods, O wise seers who behold men, O Kuśikas, drink the Soma-mead.
Come hither, O Kuśikas, take heed! Release the horse of Sudās for the sake of wealth.
May the King slay Vṛtra—east, west, and north—and then let him sacrifice at the best place upon the earth.
I have praised Indra, who sustains both these worlds, heaven and earth;
this prayer of Viśvāmitra protects the Bharata people.
The Viśvāmitras have offered this prayer to Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt;
may he indeed make us richly bountiful.
What do your cows do among the Kīkaṭas? They do not yield the milk-mixture, nor do they heat the *gharma* vessel.
Bring to us the wealth of Pramaganda; O Maghavan, subject the Naicāśākha to us.
Sasarparī, dispelling ignorance, has lowed loudly; she was given by Jamadagni. The daughter of the Sun has extended her fame among the gods—immortal and ageless.
Sasarparī quickly brought glory for them among the five peoples;
she, the winged one, bestowing new life, whom the Palastis and Jamadagnis gave to me.
May the two oxen be firm; may the axle be strong; may the two rams not push apart the pole, nor may the yoke break asunder.
May Indra protect the two side-pieces of the chariot; O you whose rim is uninjured, attend to us.
Bestow strength upon our bodies, O Indra; bestow strength upon our horses.
Bestow strength upon our children and grandchildren so that they may live, for you are indeed the giver of strength.
Envelop yourself in the essence of the *khadira* wood; bestow vigor upon the *spandana* and the *śiṃśapā*. O axle, be firm; being firm, hold us steady; do not let us slip away from this journey.
May this Lord of the Forest not abandon us, nor may he harm us;
may there be well-being for us from our homes until we reach our dwelling and our release.
O Indra, with your many and most excellent aids, quicken us today, O Maghavan, O hero!
May he who hates us fall low; may our life-breath abandon him whom we hate.
He heats even the axe and hews even the *śimbala* tree;
O Indra, even the cauldron, boiling and overflowing, casts up foam.
O people, they do not understand the arrow; thinking it to be a mere beast, they lead away the red one.
They do not cause the swift horse to run with the prize; they lead the donkey in front of the horses.
O Indra, these sons of Bharata understand only the act of sending away, not that of driving forward.
They urge on their own horse as if it were a stranger's; they lead the prize-winning steed around in the race.
For the great assembly, they have repeatedly brought forth this strength for him who is worthy of praise;
may Agni hear us with his domestic faces, and may the eternal Agni hear us with his celestial ones.
I sing a great hymn to the great Heaven and to the Earth; my desire moves about, seeking and knowing.
In the praises of these two at the assemblies, the gods, full of reverence, rejoice together with them.
O Heaven and Earth, may your cosmic order be truth; be present for our great and excellent prosperity.
This homage to Heaven and to Earth, O Agni, I offer with nourishment; I seek a treasure.

For indeed, O you two ancient and truth-abiding worlds, those who speak the word of truth have found you both; even men, seeking to gain wealth in the clash of heroes, have celebrated you, O Earth, as they sought your favor.
Who truly knows? Who here can declare it? Whither do these paths converge toward the gods?
Their lowest seats have been seen, yet they are in the highest, secret ordinances.
The seer, who beholds men, has looked upon them as they rejoice in the wide-spread womb of *ṛta*;
they have made their dwelling apart like a bird, yet they are in harmony through a common purpose.
Though distinct yet common, dwelling far apart, they stand upon a firm and watchful station;
though becoming sisters and young women, they nevertheless proclaim their names as a pair.
All these generations are clearly distinguished; though bearing the great gods, she does not waver.
The one moves, yet rules all that is firm; the winged bird flies hither and thither, born in manifold ways.

I have come from afar to this ancient kinship of ours, established of old by our great Father, the Progenitor— the kinship in which the gods, being praised with their rites, stood upon the wide, diverging path between the two worlds.

I proclaim this hymn of praise, O Heaven and Earth; may those whose hearts are soft and whose tongue is Agni hear it—the sovereign Mitra, Varuṇa the youthful, and the Ādityas, the far-extending sages.
Savitar, the golden-handed one with the beautiful tongue, who rules over the assembly three times from heaven—
O Savitar, having sent forth your renown among the gods, grant us complete well-being.
May the skillful, fair-handed, well-armed, and righteous divine Tvaṣṭṛ grant us those things for our protection.
O Ṛbhus, rejoice together with Pūṣan; having set the pressing-stones upright, you have fashioned the sacrifice.
The Maruts, with lightning-chariots, armed with spears, the youths of heaven, born of *ṛta*, tireless;
may Sarasvatī and the worshipful ones hear us—may the swift ones bestow wealth along with heroic sons.
Hymns and songs of praise go forth to Viṣṇu, the one who is seen in many places, as singers go on the path of Bhaga;
he is the wide-striding, preeminent one, whose many youthful mothers do not neglect him.
Indra, ruling through all his heroic powers, has filled both worlds with his greatness.
O breaker of forts, slayer of Vṛtra, leader of bold armies, gather and bring to us abundant cattle.

The Nāsatyas are my fathers, inquiring after kinship; the Aśvins' name is dear as a kinsman. For you two are the bestowers of wealth upon us; O undeceived ones, you protect the gift of riches with those who are not stingy.
O sages, that great and beautiful name of yours is truly yours, O All-Gods, in that you abide in Indra.
O Much-invoked One, as a friend with your dear R̥bhus, fashion this prayer of ours for the winning of the prize.
May Aryaman, Aditi, and the worshipful ones [protect us]; unassailable are the laws of Varuṇa.
Keep far from us all that leads to childlessness; may our path be rich in offspring and cattle.
May the messenger of the gods, sent forth in many ways, declare us sinless in our complete well-being.
May the Earth, the Sky, and the Waters hear us, as well as the Sun with the constellations and the vast intermediate space.
May the bull-like mountains hear us, they who are firm in their stability and rejoice in the sacrificial food;
may Aditi with the Ādityas hear us, and may the Maruts grant us auspicious protection.
May the path always be easy to traverse and rich in nourishment; O gods, sprinkle the plants with honey.
O Agni, may Bhaga not fail me in your friendship; may I attain the dwelling of wealth abounding in food.
Taste the oblations; shine forth with nourishments toward us; measure out for us glorious renown.
O Agni, conquer all those enemies in battles; shine upon us with a benevolent mind throughout all days.
When the first dawns shone forth, the great imperishable syllable was born in the station of the Cow.
As he now upholds the ordinances of the gods, the sovereignty of the gods—great and unique—is manifest.
O Agni, may the gods not lead us astray here, nor the ancient fathers who know the path.
Between the two ancient dwellings, you are the banner; great is the singular sovereignty of the gods.
My desires fly forth in many directions; I have looked toward the ancient rites with focused mind.
When the fire is kindled, let us proclaim the Truth; great is the singular divine sovereignty of the gods.
The common king, distributed in many places, lies among the resting ones, moving through the woods;
one mother bears the calf and dwells [therein]. Great is the unique sovereignty of the gods.

Dwelling in the former ones, he has grown up within the latter; as soon as they are born, he is within the young ones. Though they are pregnant, they give birth without being impregnated—great indeed is the singular divine power of the gods.
The calf, having two mothers, wanders alone, unbound, though lying far away;
these are the ordinances of Mitra and Varuṇa—the great, singular sovereignty of the gods.

The Hotṛ priest with two mothers, the sovereign in the assemblies, moves along the front while his foundation remains at rest. Those who speak pleasant words bring forth delightful offerings; great indeed is the singular divine power of the gods.
As if facing an enemy in close combat, the hero, everything approaching him is seen; the thought moves within, warding off the cow. Great is the unique sovereignty of the gods.
The gray messenger stirs within; great, he moves among these [beings] with his radiant light. Bearing wondrous forms, he looks upon us; great is the singular divine sovereignty of the gods.
Viṣṇu, the guardian, protects the supreme domain, upholding the beloved, immortal abodes.
Agni knows all those worlds; great is the singular divine sovereignty of the gods.

The twin sisters have fashioned their forms diversely; of these two, one shines black and the other is dark. When the sister who is dusky and the sister who is ruddy [meet], great is the singular divine power of the gods.
Where the Mother and the Daughter, both cows yielding nectar, suckle together;
in that seat of the Cosmic Order (Ṛta), I praise you—the singular, great lordship of the gods.
Licking the calf of another, she has lowed; with what world has the cow laid down her udder?
She, the *ilā*, swells with the milk of *ṛta*; great is the singular sovereignty of the gods.
She clothes herself in many forms; standing erect, she licks a three-year-old calf.
Knowing the seat of Cosmic Order, I move about it; great is the singular sovereignty of the gods.
Like two tracks set down by a wonder-worker, one of these is hidden within, the other is manifest;
that path leads in both directions. Great is the singular sovereignty of the gods.
Let the milch-cows come lowing—the barren ones, those that yield nectar, the restless, and those never milked.
Becoming ever new and youthful, great indeed is the singular divine power of the gods.
When the bull bellows among other herds, he deposits his seed in another herd;
for he is the protector of the night, he is Bhaga, he is the King—great is the singular divine sovereignty of the gods.
O people, let us now proclaim the hero’s possession of noble horses; the gods know this.
Drawn by six sets of five each, they carry him. Great indeed is the singular divine power of the gods.
The divine Tvaṣṭṛ, the impeller, possessing all forms, has nourished the creatures and brought them forth in many ways;
and all these worlds belong to him. Great indeed is the singular sovereignty of the gods.
The two great worlds, joined together, have been filled by him with wealth; both of them are overflowing with his riches.
The Hero is renowned for finding treasures; great indeed is the singular sovereignty of the gods.
And this earth of ours, the all-sustainer, dwells like a king with Mitra as his ally;
like heroes seated in their strongholds, the gods possess one great power of the Asuras.
The plants and the waters are yours to ward off [evil]; O Indra, the earth bears wealth for you.
May we, your friends, be sharers of your bounty; great is the singular divine sovereignty of the gods.
Neither the crafty nor the wise violate those first firm decrees of the gods. Neither the two worlds, free from malice, nor the mountains that stand firm can bend them down by their wondrous powers.
One, moving not, bears six burdens; the kine have approached the highest Truth. Three great ones stand above; two are hidden in secret, one is visible.
The bull with three faces, possessing all forms, and with three udders, manifold and rich in offspring;
he who has three armies rules as the majestic lord—he is the seed-bestowing bull of all eternal things.
The path-finder has awakened to meet them; I have invoked the beloved name of the Ādityas.
Even the divine waters paused for him; though flowing in separate directions, they turned around him.
The rivers have three abodes; the sages likewise [have three]; and the one with three mothers is the sovereign in the assemblies.
Three are the faithful maidens, the waters, who thrice from heaven preside over the assembly.

O Savitṛ, three times from heaven, day after day, impel desirable things toward us; thrice during the day, O Bhaga, bestow upon us wealth of three kinds and treasures for our gain, O Protector, O Dhīṣaṇā.
Three times from heaven Savitṛ impels [his gifts]; the two kings Mitra and Varuṇa, the fair-handed, [impel them].
Even the waters and the two wide worlds beg for wealth at the impulse of Savitṛ.
Three times the highest, difficult to overcome, are the luminous realms; three heroes of the Asura rule over them.
May the gods—upholders of *ṛta*, impetuous, and invincible—be present at the sacrifice three times from heaven.

He who discerns has found my inspired thought, like a cow wandering at large, unattended and without a herdsman—she who has straightway yielded much nourishment to drink; Indra and Agni are her praisers.
Indra and Pūṣan, the two bulls with skillful hands, being pleased like [the gods] of heaven, have milked out the inexhaustible [treasure].
Since all the gods rejoice in this [earth], O Vasus, may I here obtain your favor.
The sisters who desire the bull’s power recognize the embryo within him while paying homage. Like lowing cows toward their calf, they move toward him who bears great beauty.
I call upon the two well-established worlds with my inspired thought, yoking the pressing-stones at the sacrifice.
These sacrificial posts of yours, which grant abundant boons to mankind, stand upright and beautiful to behold, O worshipful ones.
O Agni, that honeyed and wise tongue of yours which is proclaimed among the gods as far-reaching—
by means of it, seat here all those worthy of worship for our protection, and cause them to drink the honeyed draughts.

O Agni, that brilliant and shimmering providence of yours which, like a stream from a mountain, swells with abundance, O God— O Jātavedas, O Vasu, grant us that benevolence which extends to all people.
The cow of the ancient one yields what is desirable; the son of the Dakṣiṇā moves within.
Bearing the light, he whose path is bright brings the radiance; the hymn of praise has awakened the Aśvins at dawn.
Well-yoked, they carry you both toward the cosmic order (*ṛta*); the sacrificial offerings rise upward like fathers.
Consume the thought of the niggardly man from us; we have made you our own—come hither!
O Wonder-workers, with well-yoked horses and a smoothly-rolling chariot, hear this cry from the pressing-stone.
Why indeed, O Aśvins, do the ancient sages say that you are the ones most swift to come back to our turning?
Take heed of us; come hither by your wondrous ways! All people, O Aśvins, invoke you.
For these honeyed draughts, mixed with milk, have been offered to you like friends at the break of dawn.
O Aśvins, through many realms indeed your praise has reached us among the people, O bounteous ones.
Come hither by the paths traveled by the gods; O wonder-workers, here are these offerings of honey for you.
Ancient is your dwelling, auspicious your friendship, and your wealth, O heroes, lies within the Jahnu river.
Renewing our auspicious friendships, may we now together, as equals, rejoice in the sweetness of the honeyed draught.
O Aśvins, you who are most skillful, together with Vāyu and his teams of horses, O youthful Nāsatyas, being of one mind,
enjoying the Soma that has passed the night, drink it without fail, O bounteous givers!
O Aśvins, abundant refreshments have come toward you, striving with unerring songs of praise;
for your chariot, born of Truth and urged by the pressing-stones, traverses heaven and earth in an instant.

O Aśvins, this Soma, most sweetly pressed, is for you; drink it and come to our dwelling. Your chariot, displaying many forms, shall come most readily to the prepared place of him who has pressed the juice.
Mitra, speaking, impels men; Mitra has supported both the earth and the sky.
Mitra gazes upon the people with unblinking eyes; offer an oblation rich in ghee unto Mitra.
O Mitra, O Āditya, let that mortal be foremost who exerts himself for you with sacred observance;
he whom you protect is neither slain nor conquered, and no distress reaches him, neither from near nor from afar.
Free from disease, rejoicing in the sacrificial food, with measured steps upon the wide expanse of the earth,
abiding in the ordinance of Āditya, may we remain in the benevolent favor of Mitra.

This Mitra, worthy of homage, most gracious, a king of noble power and a wise ordainer, has been born. May we abide in the favor of that one worthy of sacrifice, and likewise in his auspicious goodwill.

The great Āditya is to be approached with homage; he who brings men together is most gracious to the one who praises him. To him, the most praiseworthy Mitra, offer this pleasing oblation into the fire.
The aid of the god Mitra, the sustainer of the people, brings gain; his glory possesses the most wonderful renown.
Mitra, who by his greatness has extended beyond the heavens, has surpassed the earth with his glorious renown.
The five peoples have submitted to Mitra for his protective power;
he sustains all the gods.
Mitra among the gods and among living beings has provided nourishment for the person who has spread the sacrificial grass, according to his desired vows.
O heroes, by your own will and through kinship, the *uśijaḥ* have come here and there with their knowledge;
by those wondrous powers (*māyā*) which manifest in various forms, you sons of Sudhanvan have obtained your share in the sacrifice.
By those powers with which you fashioned the chalices, by that insight through which you brought forth the cow from the hide,
and by that mind with which you wrought the two bay steeds— by all this, O Ṛbhus, you attained divinity.
The Ṛbhus attained the friendship of Indra; the sons of Manu, the skillful workers, hastened forth.
The sons of Sudhanvan won immortality, having performed their labors with sacred rites, being doers of good through their skillful work.
With Indra you go on the same chariot to the pressed juice; thus, together with your splendor, you become the masters of desires.
O Ṛbhus, sons of Sudhanvan, your well-wrought deeds and heroic exploits have no equals among those who offer sacrifice.
O Indra, together with the R̥bhus who possess strength, pour down the pressed Soma sprinkled in your two hands.
Urged by our prayer, O Maghavan, rejoice in the house of the donor together with the sons of Sudhanvan, those heroes.
O Indra, accompanied by the *Ṛbhus* and the *Vājins*, rejoice here at this libation for us, O you who are praised with many hymns, through your power.
These pastures have been offered to you; the ordinances of the gods and the laws of men have been established according to their statutes.
O Indra, together with the Ribhus, the swift ones, seeking booty, come here to the worshipful hymn of the singer;
with a hundred vigorous impulses for the sake of the living man, you who have a thousand ways, come to the offering of the sacrifice.
O Dawn, rich in booty, wise one, accept with favor the hymn of the singer, O bountiful lady!
Ancient yet youthful goddess, possessor of abundance, you move according to the sacred law, O you who grant all boons.
O immortal goddess Uṣas, shine forth with your moon-bright chariot, sending out pleasant songs.
Let the well-governed horses of broad luster bring you here—you who are golden-hued.
O Dawn, facing all beings, you stand upright as the banner of immortality;
pursuing your common purpose, turn hither like a wheel, O ever-new one.
Like one drawing out a thread, the bounteous Uṣas comes, the mistress of the dwelling;
generating light, the fortunate and wondrous one has spread from the end of heaven across the earth.
Bring forth with reverence your hymn of praise toward the radiant goddess Uṣas.
The honey-bearer has established her splendor high in heaven; she of lovely aspect has shone forth through the luminous realms.
O observer of the cosmic order, you have been awakened by the hymns of heaven; the wealthy one has risen with splendor across both worlds.
O Agni, seeking desirable wealth, you go toward the approaching, radiant Dawn.
Stirring the dawns at the foundation of Cosmic Order, the Bull has entered the two great worlds, heaven and earth.
Great is the creative power (*māyā*) of Mitra and Varuṇa; like the moon, it has distributed its light in many places.
These longings of ours, which we have cherished, have not been too much for one like you;
where, O Indra and Varuṇa, is that glory of yours by which you bring wealth to your friends?
This man, seeking wealth, repeatedly invokes you both most frequently for protection.
O Indra and Varuṇa, being of one mind with the Maruts, hear my call from heaven and earth.

O Indra and Varuṇa, may that wealth be ours; O Maruts, may there be for us riches consisting of all heroic sons. May the Varūtrīs protect us with their shelters; may Hotrā Bhāratī protect us with sacrificial gifts.
O Bṛhaspati, who belongs to all the gods, enjoy our oblations;
bestow jewels upon the donor.
Worship the pure Bṛhaspati with hymns at the sacrifices;
he has willed his unbending might.
Bṛhaspati, the bull of the people, possessing every form, the invincible and most excellent one.
O Pūṣan, O glowing god, this newest hymn of praise for you is being recited by us to you.
Accept this my song that strives for booty; favor my prayer as a suitor favors a young woman.
May that Pūṣan, who gazes upon all beings and beholds them together, be our protector.
We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ;
may he impel our thoughts.
Seeking strength through the wisdom of Purandhi, we pray for the gift of Bhaga from the god Savitṛ.
The sages, impelled by their devotion, worship the divine Savitṛ with sacrifices and well-fashioned hymns.
Soma goes forth, knowing the way; he goes to the appointed place of the gods, to sit in the womb of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
May Soma provide for us, for our bipeds and for our four-footed livestock,
food free from disease.
Increasing our lifespan and overcoming adversaries,
Soma has taken his seat in the common dwelling place.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter; O you of noble wisdom, drench the regions with honey.
O you of wide renown, strengthened by homage, you rule through the greatness of skill; with your most far-reaching [powers], O you whose vows are pure.
Being praised by Jamadagni, sit upon the seat of Cosmic Order;
drink the Soma, O you who increase the Truth!
